drafted_from: tool:save-a-form's own row (its words and input schema) and what its tool answered when run against a real PostgreSQL server (test/form-tools.test.mjs); read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Check a form, a list of questions people answer, and keep it in the person's own database, so it can be asked and its answers checked", with {"form_id":"sample-intake","title":"Sample intake","questions":[{"questionId":"budget","questionTypeId":"number","label":"Budget"}]}. It runs tool:save-a-form and answers {"form_id":"sample-intake","record_id":"question-sequence:sample-intake","question_count":1,"record":{"id":"question-sequence:sample-intake","type":"question-sequence","value":{"kind":"question-sequence","formId":"sample-intake","title":"Sample intake","questions":[{"questionId":"budget","questionTypeId":"number","label":"Budget"}]}}}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it keeps its rows in tables of your own database, reached only on the local port your computer reports as own-rows-postgres.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Check a form, a list of questions people answer, and keep it in the person's own database, so it can be asked and its answers checked", and give it form_id (the form's name, kept in the row id); questions (the questions, in order).
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @tools with method tools:run, tool tool:save-a-form and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Each question needs a questionId and a questionTypeId (a row in the question-type list: text, long text, number, rating, choice, a reference to a file) and may carry a label, required, options, its own validation rules laid over its type's, and an afterSaved hand-off naming an owner and an action. The form is kept as one row of the table question_sequence (the same form_id replaces the same row) and answered with how many questions it holds.
4. It keeps its rows in tables of your own database, reached only on the local port your computer reports as own-rows-postgres.
